sentences.latin: Numquam sum magis de occupationibus meis questus, quae me non sunt passae aut proficiscentem te valetudinis causa in Campaniam prosequi aut profectam e vestigio subsequi.
sentences.english: Never have I complained more about my own duties, which did not allow me either to accompany you as you set out for Campania for your health, or to follow you immediately after you had set out.

sentences.latin: Nunc enim praecipue simul esse cupiebam, ut oculis meis crederem quid viribus quid corpusculo apparares, ecquid denique secessus voluptates regionisque abundantiam inoffensa transmitteres.
sentences.english: For now especially I was longing to be with you, so that I might trust my own eyes about what you were managing for your strength, what for your dear body, and finally whether you were getting through the pleasures of your retreat and the abundance of the region without trouble.

sentences.latin: Equidem etiam fortem te non sine cura desiderarem; est enim suspensum et anxium de eo quem ardentissime diligas interdum nihil scire.
sentences.english: Indeed I should miss you, even when strong, not without anxiety; for it is suspenseful and worrying to know nothing for a time about one whom you love most ardently.

sentences.latin: Nunc vero me cum absentiae tum infirmitatis tuae ratio incerta et varia sollicitudine exterret.
sentences.english: But now the thought both of your absence and of your illness alarms me with uncertain and varied worry.

sentences.latin: Vereor omnia, imaginor omnia, quaeque natura metuentium est, ea maxime mihi quae maxime abominor fingo.
sentences.english: I fear everything, I imagine everything, and as is the nature of those who are afraid, I picture to myself most vividly the very things I most dread.

sentences.latin: Quo impensius rogo, ut timori meo cottidie singulis vel etiam binis epistulis consulas.
sentences.english: Therefore I beg you all the more earnestly to attend to my fear daily by one or even two letters.

sentences.latin: Ero enim securior dum lego, statimque timebo cum legero.
sentences.english: For I shall be more at ease while I read, and shall fear again as soon as I have finished reading.
